call.target_note: the callee at 0x3c1ada0 IS an FDE start (1070 bytes, .eh_frame+0x00509b84, cie 0x0022d474), but its body is excluded here and its result is ignored: on the fast path the window overwrites rax with mov al, 1 before returning, so no claim about the callee's computation is made

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

function.padding_note: five int3 bytes (0xcc) at [0x3bde10b, 0x3bde110) pad the window to the next FDE at 0x3bde110

edges.note: zero records: vacuous all-nonzero, returns 1 without scanning
three records, all flags nonzero returns 1
middle record flag zero returns 0 (early exit)
10000 records, just below the threshold, scan path with all flags nonzero returns 1
10000 records, just below the threshold, scan path with a zero flag returns 0
10001 records, exactly at the threshold: fast path, returns 1 without scanning
10002 records, above the threshold: fast path, returns 1 even if some flags were zero

rule.formula: if count >= 10001 (unsigned): write u16 0x143 to a stack slot, call callee(stack_slot), ignore the result, return 1 in al; else: return 1 in al iff every byte at records_base + i*80 + 0x4e is nonzero for i in 0..count-1, else 0 in al (count 0 returns 1 vacuously)
rule.formula_note: the threshold compare is unsigned (jb); the scan checks the flag byte at offset 0x4e of each 80-byte record in forward order and exits early on the first zero byte; the verdict is delivered in al only (the upper bytes of rax are not normalized by the verdict instructions), so the rule is stated over al; the fast-path callee argument is the address of the stack slot holding 0x143, and the callee result is overwritten by mov al, 1 before the return
rule.inputs: count (u64 at input struct + 0x10), records_base (pointer at input struct + 0x08), flags (bytes at records_base + i*80 + 0x4e), fast-path slot value (u16 0x143 = 323)
